cards.text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster, to be played with stringed instruments. David opens with a prayer: "Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness!" And this isn't his first time calling. He's got history with God.

cards.question: David reminds God of something He's already done for him. What is it?
True or false: David goes on to ask God to show him grace and hear his prayer.

cards.text: Then David turns from God to people: "How long, O men, will my honor be maligned?" And then he asks How long AGAIN. I think David has had it UP to here.

cards.question: True or false: In his second How long question, David says those men love the truth and seek after it.

cards.text: Vanity and lies. That's what they're chasing. But David's not done with them. He tells those men there's something they need to know about the LORD.

cards.question: David wants those men to know what the LORD has done with the godly. What is it?

answers.text: Made them rulers of the land
Sent them out to the nations

cards.question: David is sure of something else too. He says the LORD ___ when he calls to Him.

cards.text: Then David gives some advice: "Be angry, yet do not sin." Notice it doesn't say never get angry.

cards.question: David says to search your heart and be still. Where?

cards.text: On your BED. Ever lie there at 2 a.m. writing the PERFECT comeback to an argument from last week? That's not searching your heart, friend. That's rehearsing round two.

cards.question: David's advice keeps going: offer the sacrifices of the righteous. What else does he say to do?

cards.text: Then David brings up a question: "Many ask, 'Who can show us the good?'" Big question. And David doesn't answer it with a name. He turns to the LORD.

cards.question: Many want someone to show them the good. David asks the LORD to shine the ___ of His face upon them.

cards.text: Now David gets personal about joy. He measures it against harvest time, when grain and new wine abound.

cards.question: True or false: David says God has filled his heart with MORE joy than when grain and new wine abound.

cards.text: A whole harvest, and God's joy BEATS it. I used to think nothing topped a full batch coming out of my oven with sharp edges, and David's over here like, hold my cookie box.

cards.question: Last line. David says he will lie down and sleep in peace. Why?

answers.text: The LORD alone keeps him safe
His enemies have all gone home
His guards are watching the door

cards.text: Friend, I spent years lying awake in the back of a junk drawer. Every rattle, I was UP. David's got men dragging his honor, and he's lying down to sleep in PEACE, because the LORD alone makes him dwell in safety.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "Be angry, yet do not sin.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "Many ask, 'Who can show us the good?'", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: the superscription, the quoted prayer, "And this isn't his first time calling." and "He's got history with God."

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: "This isn't his first time calling" stretches the text. Psalm 4:1 says God has relieved David's distress, but it never says David called on Him before.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The story card has 3 sentences: the quoted question, "And then he asks How long AGAIN." and "I think David has had it UP to here."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: "Vanity and lies.", "That's what they're chasing.", "But David's not done with them." and "He tells those men..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "sleeps" (the LORD sleeps when David calls) is silly and easy to rule out. It doesn't match the tone of the other answers, so "hears" stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Cards 9 and 12 call David's commands in Psalm 4:4-5 "advice." The text gives them as commands ("Be angry, yet do not sin", "Offer...", "trust...") and never calls them advice.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card is only a joke about verse 4, which cards 9 and 10 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: "On your BED.", the 2 a.m. question, "That's not searching your heart, friend." and "That's rehearsing round two."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "David doesn't answer it with a name. He turns to the LORD." presents the prayer in Psalm 4:6 as David's answer to the question. The text sets the two side by side and never says how they connect. "Doesn't answer it with a name" is also an odd claim, since "the LORD" is a name.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: the quoted question, "Big question.", "And David doesn't answer it with a name." and "He turns to the LORD."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: With "shine the ___ of His face," the wrong answers "shadow" and "frown" don't fit the verb "shine." They read as silly, and "light" stands out as the only answer that works.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card only reacts to verse 7, which cards 15 and 16 already covered. It restates that God's joy beats the harvest and tells no new part of the passage.
The card restates the verse 8 answer from card 18 ("because the LORD alone makes him dwell in safety") and calls back to verse 2. It tells no new part of the passage.
The story card has 3 sentences: "Friend, I spent years lying awake...", "Every rattle, I was UP." and "David's got men dragging his honor..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
